HomeRobot.collection: A collection of the robots I worked with

robots.name: P-Guard
mission: Security patrols.
Intrusions and/or anomalies detection via AI.
Doubt removals with video verification and remote interpellation.
On-demand intervention.
« Click and Go » function.
Real-time remote control of the robot with anti-collision safety.
hardware: 360° camera for object segmentation and remote monitoring
4 wheels actuators with encoders for differential-drive motion

robots.name: S-Drone
mission: Underwater exploration/inspection drone.
Automated scanning of cargo hull and analysis report generation via AI.
Pipe exploration and leakage detection.
Seabed scanning and object retrieval.
Position fixing (altitude, distance...) via numerical controllers.
Real-time video feedback and remote control in every direction.

robots.name: S-Navigator
mission: Surface Wi-Fi relay.
Combines the GPS absolute position and acoustic relative position to locate the underwater robot down to cm-level precision.
Automated bathymetric survey with complete coverage path-planning algorithms.
« Click and Go » function.
Real-time remote control via vector-state feedback controllers.
hardware: 3 propellers for 3 degrees of freedom and holonomic motion

robots.name: UR5e
mission: Industrial, collaborative robot.
Used for research on cooking robots and soft manipulation.
A camera segments vegetables on the cutting plane, the first arm picks it up and holds it, and the second cuts it.
The motion of the knife is handled by a Q-Learning Policy trained to minimize the force/torque exerted on it.
hardware: Coupled with virtual twins for reinforcement learning processes

robots.name: B1A
mission: Autonomous cleaning of land-based solar panels to maximize the energy production.
Executes a succession of maneuvers to accomplish a cleaning mission ordered by the operator via the web interface.
Segmentation of the panels shapes and positions with the LiDARs and RANSAC models.
Bringing down the brush and self-regulating cleaning pressure to optimize the cleaning.
hardware: 3D LiDARs for panel segmentation and obstacle avoidance
6 wheels actuators with encoders for holonomic motion
Sonars, winches encoders and limit switches for brush regulation

robots.name: F1T
mission: Autonomous cleaning of floating solar panels to maximize the energy production.
Developed under the scope of the Horizon Europe project 'Talos'.
Switching behavior automatically depending on the conditions of the photovoltaic plant to clean when / where needed.
Segmentation of the panels' centroid with the depth cameras and custom YOLO model.
hardware: Framos depth cameras for panel segmentation and obstacle avoidance
2 tracked wheel actuators for differential-drive motion

HomeModal.welcome: Welcome to the homepage help corner !​
HomeModal.subtitle1: In this webpage, you can have a brief overview of who I am as well as the robots I worked on.
HomeModal.subtitle2: This project is still work-in-progress. UI/UX design is not my specialty but as you can (hopefully) see, I am doing my best and having a blast while doing so !
HomeModal.contact: The 'contact me' button opens your mail application with my pre-filled address.
HomeModal.download: The 'download CV' button downloads a PDF of my CV on your device.
HomeModal.visit: The 'visit the lab' button routes your browser to my online ROS2 laboratory.
HomeModal.3d: The 3D medalion is orbitable if you left-lick and drag on it.
HomeModal.robots: Clicking on the number of developped robot will transfer you to the robot carousel section of the page.
HomeModal.scrolldown: Furthermore, the page automatically scrolls down to the robot carousel when you use your mouse wheel.
HomeModal.arrow: The left and right arrow buttons rotate the robot in the carousel.
HomeModal.picture: You can also go to a specific robot by clicking on its displayed picture.
HomeModal.card: The robot card opens a tab with the commercial description of the selected robot.
HomeModal.media: The media card contains a youtube video player with a small demo of the robot.
HomeModal.hardware: The hardware card contains a short description of the sensors equipping the robot.
HomeModal.missions: The missions card contains a non-exhaustive list of the robot's features.
HomeModal.shift: You can shift cards by clicking on it.
HomeModal.scrollup: Finally, the page automatically scrolls up to the about me section when you use your mouse wheel.

LabModal.welcome: Welcome to the laboratory help corner !
LabModal.subtitle1: In this online laboratory, you can play with some robots that are being simulated in Gazebo on a remote server.
LabModal.subtitle2: Everything runs on ROS2, open-source packages and custom JS/C++ code.
LabModal.ros: The ROS connection lightbulb is green if the rosbridge websocket has connected, red otherwise.
LabModal.controller: The Controller connection lightbulb is green if a game controller is connected, red otherwise.
LabModal.switch: You can switch the camera feed by clicking on 'robot view' and 'aerial view'.
LabModal.choice: The 'apply choice' button is still WIP.
LabModal.operate: To operate the robot, play with the joystick displayed in the main frame.
LabModal.reset: You can reset the position of the robot in the world by pressing 'reset'.
LabModal.connected: If you connected a controller to your device, you can also use it.
LabModal.pan: You can pan the data graph by left clicking + holding it, pause it, and reset it to the default view.
LabModal.rescale: You can rescale the temporal axis by scrolling on the graph.
LabModal.hover: Hovering your mouse over the graph will display the numerical values of each point.
LabModal.orbit: You can use orbit control to rotate around and zoom on the virtual twin.
LabModal.data: You can switch the data stream by clicking on 'focus on:'.
